source.version: NBER Working Paper 33641, April 2025 (title ends 'Generative AI Reshaping Teamwork and Expertise'). The latest version is the Organization Science article (2026, doi 10.1287/orsc.2025.20702), whose abstract gives N = 791 per the search record; this NBER version's text says 776.
source.title_on_document: The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI Reshaping Teamwork and Expertise

supplement.where: Appendix A (problem statements), B (evaluation process), C (prompts) and Figure A1 sit at pp. 47-54 of this PDF.
supplement.holds: The appendix in this PDF holds no statistics beyond Figure A1. Footnote 11 (p. 13) says the replication with AI-generated evaluations is 'shown in Appendix', but no such result appears in this PDF. Results for novelty, feasibility, impact, and business potential are not printed anywhere in this PDF (p. 11 only says they 'confirm the findings').

paper_design_summary: In a preregistered one-day virtual product-development workshop at Procter & Gamble (May-July 2024), professionals were randomly assigned in a 2x2 design to work alone or in a cross-functional two-person team (one R&D, one Commercial), with or without a GPT-4-based tool. Each individual or team submitted one solution to a real business-unit problem. Blind evaluators rated the 550 solutions on overall quality (primary), novelty, feasibility, and technicality, and the paper also reports length, time, top-10% quality, semantic similarity across solutions, and self-reported emotions.

studies.label: P&G field experiment (2x2: individual/team x no AI/AI), new product development task

assignment.what_was_assigned: Individual participants to one of four conditions: individual without AI (control), team without AI (T1), individual with AI (T2), team with AI (T3); teams formed by randomly pairing one Commercial and one R&D professional.
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to these conditions within each of the eight randomization clusters, defined by four business units (Baby Care, Feminine Care, Grooming, and Oral Care) across two geographies (Europe and Americas).
assignment.locator: p. 9, Section 3.2; p. 10 (stratification, random pairing); p. 29, Figure 1
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 2 (AEA RCT registry trials/13603); p. 8, footnote 3 (AEARCTR-0013603)

arms.name: Team No AI (T1)
arms.description: Two-person team (R&D + Commercial) without GenAI; 115 teams.

arms.name: Individual + AI (T2)
arms.description: Works alone with the GPT-4-based tool after a one-hour prompting training.

arms.name: Team + AI (T3)
arms.description: Two-person team (R&D + Commercial) with the GPT-4-based tool after the training; 126 teams.

participants.exclusions: 811 took part in the workshop; 35 were not randomly assigned (late entrants did the task alone without AI; those above band 3 did it alone with AI) and are excluded (p. 9, fn 6). The text says analyses focus on 776 randomized participants, but Table 1 arm counts (154 + 155 + 230 + 252) sum to 791 people, and these arms match the 550 solutions in the regressions (154 + 155 + 115 + 126). The paper does not explain the 776 vs 791 gap. Footnote 8 says individuals from teams whose partner failed to participate were reassigned to individual conditions after randomization; the number is not stated. n_analyzed = 791 is the sum of Table 1 arm counts.
participants.who: Experienced Commercial and R&D professionals at Procter & Gamble in four business units, enrolled through an organizational upskilling program.
participants.quote: The experiment was conducted as a one-day virtual product development workshop, involving 811 participants from P&G's Commercial and R&D functions. Our analyses focus on 776 of these participants who were randomly assigned across four conditions.
participants.locator: p. 9, Section 3.2 and footnote 6; p. 41, Table 1

ai_tool.name_model: GenAI tool built on GPT-4, accessed through Microsoft Azure; July workshop participants had GPT-4o.
ai_tool.how_used: Free use of a chat tool during the task, after a one-hour training led by an author with a PDF of recommended prompts (ideation, framing, simulated customer interview, research prompts; Appendix C). Team members collaborated over Microsoft Teams with one randomly designated member sharing the screen and submitting. Control groups later received the training and repeated the task with AI (crossover), but the paper reports no results from that second round.

task.description: Develop a new solution (product, packaging, communication, or retail execution idea) for a real business need of the participant's business unit; four problem statements in Appendix A. Submissions had an idea name, recommended solution, rationale, critical work required, and resources needed.
task.duration: One-day virtual workshop; task time not stated as a fixed limit (time spent is an outcome, Table 4).

outcomes.name: Solution quality (standardized)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Overall quality on a 1-10 scale ('A comprehensive assessment of the solution's merit'), rated by 22 evaluators blind to condition (MBA and Engineering students or recent graduates at a top business or engineering school), 1,595 evaluations, about 2.89 per solution, averaged per solution; ICC2 0.452. Standardized on the individual-no-AI control group. Three specifications: no controls; business-unit and date FE; FE plus controls. Robust SEs. Subgroups by core vs non-core job in Table 5. The paper calls this its primary outcome; it is a quality rating, not a creativity rating (the codebook puts quality under usefulness).

contrasts.reported: Individual + AI 0.373*** (0.106) [no controls]; 0.386*** (0.108) [FE]; 0.370*** (0.107) [FE + controls]. Control mean 0.000 (0.081). Observations 550. Text: 0.37 SD (p < 0.01). Table 5: non-core 0.324** (0.149), core 0.433*** (0.152) [Model 1].
contrasts.locator: p. 42, Table 2; p. 14, Section 5.1; p. 30, Figure 2; p. 43, Table 5

outcomes.name: Top 10% quality solution
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Binary: 1 if the solution's quality score (1-10) is in the highest decile across all submissions. Linear probability model, three specifications.

contrasts.locator: p. 46, Table 10; p. 37, Figure 9; p. 17, Section 6.1

outcomes.name: Semantic similarity between solutions (distance from mean)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Kernel densities of each solution's 'Distance from Mean (Squared Units)' within its condition, from sentence embeddings and cosine distance; lower values mean higher similarity. Also compared with an 'AI Only' set of GPT-4o solutions to the same problems.

contrasts.reported: Diversity lower with AI (sign reversed from similarity). Text: 'AI-aided solutions demonstrate notably higher semantic similarity.' Figure 13 shows densities only: Alone + AI and Pair + AI peak near 0.6, Alone and Pair near 0.7. No means, SEs, or tests.

contrasts.control_arm: AI Only (GPT-4o prompted with the problem instructions)
contrasts.reported: 'This "AI Only" shows much tighter clustering'; AI Only density peaks near 0.33. AI-aided solutions are more dispersed than AI Only. No statistics.
contrasts.locator: p. 19, Section 6.4 and footnote 14; p. 40, Figure 13

diversity_detail.metric: Distance from the condition mean in embedding space (squared units); notes also say cosine distance between solutions
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each solution against the mean (centroid) of its condition's solutions
diversity_detail.uncertainty: None reported; kernel density plot only
diversity_detail.notes: Number of AI Only solutions not stated. Figure notes describe both 'distance from mean' and 'cosine distance between solutions', so the exact computation is ambiguous.

outcomes.name: Solution length (words)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Total number of words in the submitted solution (computed count; no creativity scoring model). Three specifications.

outcomes.name: Technicality of solution (technical vs commercial orientation)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 Likert score by the same evaluators; higher = more technically oriented, lower = more commercially oriented. Reported as density plots by participant function (individuals) and by team condition, plus bimodality coefficients for teams.

contrasts.reported: Without AI, Commercial participants' solutions are less technical than R&D participants'; with AI the two distributions look similar. No statistics.
Bimodality coefficient = 0.564 (Team No AI) vs 0.482 (Team + AI); 'similar overall levels of technical content.'

outcomes.name: Novelty
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-10 scale, 'the degree of innovation and originality', rated with the quality score by the same blind evaluators. Described as a robustness check; no results printed.

contrasts.reported: No numbers. Text: 'we also collected information on solution novelty, feasibility, and impact as robustness checks. These measures confirm the findings reported in the main text.' Direction rests only on this sentence.
contrasts.locator: p. 11, Section 3.2; p. 13, Section 4.2; p. 48, Appendix B.3

outcomes.name: Feasibility
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-10 scale, 'how practical and implementable the solutions are'. Robustness check; no results printed.

contrasts.reported: No numbers; p. 11 says the robustness measures 'confirm the findings reported in the main text.'
contrasts.locator: p. 11, Section 3.2; p. 13, Section 4.2; p. 48, Appendix B.3

outcomes.name: Impact and business potential
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Impact ('effectiveness in addressing the problem and creating value') and Business Potential, each on a 1-10 scale (Appendix B.3). Impact is named as a robustness check on p. 11; business potential is mentioned only in Appendix B.3. No results printed for either.

contrasts.reported: No numbers; p. 11 says novelty, feasibility, and impact 'confirm the findings reported in the main text.' Nothing is said about business potential results.

company_involvement.description: Four coauthors (Yi Han, Jeff Goldman, Hari Nair, Stewart Taub) list Procter & Gamble affiliations. P&G provided financial support to the Digital Data Design Institute through gifts to HBS in 2023-2025, and Karim Lakhani was a paid consultant for P&G in 2021-2022. The experiment ran inside P&G with real business problems. No AI-company involvement is stated.

eligibility.reason: Individuals were randomly assigned (stratified by business unit and geography) to work with or without a GPT-4 tool on an idea-generation task (p. 9). 776 randomized per text, 791 in Table 1 arms, so far above 50 people; the cleanest contrast (Individual + AI 155 vs Individual No AI 154) alone has 309 people. Blind evaluators scored each solution, and the paper reports semantic similarity across solutions (Figure 13). Caveat: the primary rated outcome is overall quality, not creativity; novelty was rated but no novelty statistics are printed, and diversity is shown only as a density plot.

one_line_finding: Individuals with AI produced solutions rated 0.37 control-group SD higher in quality than individuals without AI (0.373, SE 0.106, Table 2, p. 42), about the level of human teams without AI, and AI-aided solutions were more semantically similar to each other (Figure 13, p. 40, no statistics).
open_questions: Participant count: text says 776 randomized and analyzed (p. 9), while Table 1 arm counts sum to 791 (p. 41), matching the 550 solutions; the journal version reportedly says 791. Which count should the record use, and does the journal version explain it?

Footnote 8 (p. 10) says members of incomplete teams were reassigned to individual conditions after randomization; the number is not stated, so the individual arms may include non-randomly reassigned people.

Construct coding of the primary outcome: overall quality (1-10, 'comprehensive assessment of the solution's merit') is coded usefulness under the codebook; should it count as overall_creativity for the primary record?
Evaluators are described as 'expert' but were MBA and Engineering students or recent graduates (Appendix B.1, p. 48); expert_raters vs human_raters.

Novelty, feasibility, impact, and the AI-generated evaluations (fn 11) are said to confirm the results, but no statistics appear in this NBER version; check whether the Organization Science version or its online appendix reports them.
Unit of analysis for quality is the solution: individual arms have one person per solution, team arms one team per solution. For T3 vs T1 the unit is the team (115 vs 126 teams).
notes: Outcomes not listed because they are not scored on the output: log time spent (Table 4), positive and negative self-reported emotions (Tables 6-9, Figures 7-8), self-reported expected quality (Figure 10), and retention of AI-generated sentences in final solutions (Figure 12, a usage measure). Control groups did a second round with AI after training (crossover, p. 11), but the paper reports no results from it, and all primary results use the first round. Robust SEs throughout; Table 2 control-mean row shows 0.000 (0.081) in col. 1. Footnote 10: July workshop used GPT-4o; results 'remain consistent'.
